title: Unit Economics Dashboard: Access Controls (Feature Flag, RBAC, Audit Logging)
author: Marcus Lin
body:
## Summary
The Unit Economics dashboard is an internal tool that exposes sensitive cost and margin-adjacent signals (e.g., GPU rate card applications, blended $/1M output tokens, allocation knobs). Access must be gated at runtime, permissioned via RBAC, and auditable.

This page documents the current enforcement model for Console UI + backend APIs, including required audit events and operational guidance.

## Scope
In scope:
- Runtime access gating using a feature flag
- RBAC permission checks for UI routes and API endpoints
- Audit logging for access attempts and changes to access

Out of scope:
- Data redaction rules inside results
- External/customer access
- Non-Console distribution of the same metrics

## Controls overview (defense in depth)
1) Feature flag gate (fail-closed)
2) RBAC permission gate
3) Audit logging for both access and administrative changes

Important: UI hiding is not sufficient. The backend must enforce all controls.

## Feature flag
### Flag configuration
- Flag name: `unit_econ_dashboard_internal`
- Default: OFF for all users (safe default)
- Enablement model:
  - Dogfood allowlist by group: Finance, Product Analytics, Platform Eng
  - Optional broader internal rollout: "All employees" only after Security + Finance sign-off (data quality and comms readiness)

### Enforcement points
- Console UI:
  - Route guard hides navigation entry
  - Direct URL access must still show a permission denied state
- Backend APIs:
  - Deny requests when the flag is OFF, even if RBAC allows
  - Enforcement must occur before any caching layer that could leak responses

### Denial behavior
- HTTP status: 403
- Stable error code: `UNIT_ECON_FORBIDDEN`
- Required reason codes:
  - `flag_off`
  - `missing_permission`

Response shape (example): `{ code: UNIT_ECON_FORBIDDEN, reason: "flag_off" }`

## RBAC
### Permissions
Current required permissions:
- `console.unit_economics.view_internal` (required to view dashboard and call read-only APIs)
- `console.unit_economics.export_internal` (required for exports/reconciliation reports)

Note: Earlier implementations treated exports as part of the view permission. As of 2025-03-01, exports must use a separate permission to reduce accidental broad access.

### Protected surfaces
Protect all of the following behind both the feature flag AND RBAC:
- UI routes for the Unit Economics dashboard
- API endpoints serving:
  - time series
  - breakdowns
  - any export endpoints / reconciliation report downloads

### UI behavior
- For denied access, UI must show:
  - “Internal-only dashboard” messaging
  - Link to the access request process (see "Access request process")
  - No data preview / partial render

## Audit logging
### Goals
We need auditable evidence for:
1) Access attempts to the dashboard (success + denied)
2) Administrative changes to who can access (feature flag allowlist changes and RBAC grants)

### Event names
Event names align to the existing audit naming convention:
- `audit.console.unit_econ.access_granted`
- `audit.console.unit_econ.access_denied`
- `audit.authz.permission_grant` and `audit.authz.permission_revoke` (Authz service standard events)
- `audit.flags.allowlist_update` (must include the flag name `unit_econ_dashboard_internal`)

### Required payload fields
Keep payload minimal and avoid customer identifiers.
Required fields:
- actor_user_id
- actor_email
- action
- timestamp
- request_id
- surface: `ui` or `api`
- route (normalized route template preferred, not full URL)
- outcome: `granted` or `denied`
- reason: `flag_off` or `missing_permission`
- ip and user_agent (only if part of the standard audit schema)

Do NOT include:
- query filters that may contain customer identifiers (e.g., customer_id)
- raw request bodies
- response payload samples

### Volume guidance
- Current policy: log access_granted/access_denied per request for Unit Economics endpoints.
- If event volume becomes excessive, Security may approve downsampling for access_granted only (access_denied should remain 1:1).

### Retention
Follow the standard internal audit retention policy. No extended retention is required specifically for Unit Economics.

## Implementation guidance (engineering)
- Enforce on the server first. UI route guards are secondary.
- Prefer a unified guard pattern:
  - `requireFeatureFlag(unit_econ_dashboard_internal)`
  - `requirePermission(console.unit_economics.view_internal)`
  - For exports: `requirePermission(console.unit_economics.export_internal)`
- Ensure caches do not bypass auth:
  - Do not cache pre-auth
  - Avoid caching 403s across users
  - If caching post-auth, include user_id (or equivalent authorization context) in cache keys

## Access request process (operational)
When an employee needs access:
1) Request in #eng-platform with:
   - Business justification
   - Role (Finance/Product/Engineering)
   - Whether export access is required
2) Platform Eng verifies manager approval for non-Finance requests.
3) Grant RBAC permissions:
   - `console.unit_economics.view_internal`
   - Add `console.unit_economics.export_internal` only if justified
4) Ensure the user (or their group) is allowlisted for `unit_econ_dashboard_internal` if the org-wide rollout is not enabled.
5) Verify audit trail exists for the grant (Authz audit event) and, if changed, allowlist update audit event.

## Acceptance checklist (for changes to this control)
- When flag OFF: all Unit Economics API calls return 403 with `UNIT_ECON_FORBIDDEN` and reason `flag_off`.
- When flag ON but permission missing: 403 with reason `missing_permission`.
- When flag ON and permission present: access works for both UI and API.
- Audit events are emitted for granted + denied access with request_id and surface.
- Permission grant/revoke events are present in the Authz audit stream.
- Allowlist updates produce an audit event referencing `unit_econ_dashboard_internal`.
- Logs contain no PII/customer identifiers in fields beyond standard actor metadata.

## Change log
- 2025-02-20: Initial publication based on the v1 internal dashboard rollout plan.
- 2025-03-01: Split export access into separate permission `console.unit_economics.export_internal`.
- 2025-03-11: Clarified payload exclusions (no query filters) and reiterated caching constraints.
